extracted.intended_audience: PR and communications professionals, corporate marketers, and press release writers
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for writing and structuring press releases to increase reach, engagement, and brand impact by using multimedia, CTAs, searchable wording, and purpose-driven framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Showcase Multimedia in Your Release
rubrics_metrics.description: Include multimedia elements — photos, infographics, videos or audio clips — in your press release to appeal to online audiences and broaden reach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most companies have engaging images and video on their websites; apply the same rules to press releases. Example: SC Johnson’s multichannel news release included 6 videos and 6 product photos. High-quality multimedia demonstrates commitment and credibility, shows the company cares about more than promotion, and lets readers choose how to digest the story (read, watch, browse images, or engage via embedded social sharing and “Learn More” links). The piece becomes a living, breathing content asset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Your Press Release to Drive Traffic to Your Blog
rubrics_metrics.description: Syndicate valuable content as a press release with a clear call-to-action back to your blog to attract new readers and convert them into followers or customers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft headlines that ‘tease’ the main takeaway and use sub-headlines to provide additional snippets that appeal to your audience. Include an infographic to increase online discoverability. The goal is to integrate press release distribution into a larger content marketing strategy so content reaches new audiences beyond current blog followers. Example: Robert Half’s release promoted survey findings and directed readers to their blog for more expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote Thought Leadership Through Press Releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Use press releases to broadcast organizational expertise (how-tos, market research, expert availability) so your organization is discoverable as a reliable source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make releases easily searchable for readers by using popular keywords and distilling findings into clear formats (e.g., infographics like Deloitte’s “CFO Signals”). Place the most surprising and relevant information high in the release, with additional context further down to appeal to both casual readers and industry experts. This positions the organization as a trusted expert.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalize Your Brand in the Release
rubrics_metrics.description: Write engaging, conversational news releases that showcase your company’s unique values and perspective to give your brand personality and differentiate it from competitors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know your target audience and reflect that understanding in tone, imagery, and content. Use multimedia elements (logo, short video, product shots) and messaging that lets the target demographic see a version of themselves. Example: Subaru’s release aligns with the adventurous/family-oriented, safety-conscious Forester buyer and uses imagery and video to reinforce that identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advocate Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bring environmental and social responsibility stories to light in your press releases to connect with consumers who care about brand values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broadcast CSR commitments via wide distribution (e.g., wire) and make releases stand out with interesting visuals, playful wording consistent with brand voice, and eye-catching bullet points outlining next steps. Example: Ben & Jerry’s combined playful copy with visuals and clear bullets about actions on single-use plastic to align with their brand identity and consumer values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include Clear Calls-to-Action (CTAs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Embed clear CTAs in your release to direct readers toward desired next steps (visit a blog, learn more, share, convert).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use buttons or ‘Learn More’ links and explicit CTAs that align with the release’s goals (traffic, signups, media inquiries). CTAs help integrate the release into a larger content marketing funnel and make it easy for readers to engage further.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft Headlines That Tease and Engage
rubrics_metrics.description: Write headlines that tease the main takeaway to reel in readers and use sub-headlines to provide more snippets of value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A teasing headline draws attention; sub-headlines and lead elements should quickly communicate the most compelling facts. Pair playful or curiosity-driven wording (where appropriate for brand voice) with clarity so the audience knows why the story matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make Releases Searchable with Keywords
rubrics_metrics.description: Use searchable keywords so readers googling topical terms find your release and associate your organization with those topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze popular keywords relevant to your news and include them (and infographics or concise data points) in prominent locations within the release. Searchable content increases discoverability among both consumers and journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Visual Details and Bullet Points to Highlight Next Steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Use visuals and eye-catching bullet points to summarize actions, commitments, or next steps so the release stands out and is scannable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bulleted highlights make it easy for readers to quickly understand the core actions or takeaways (e.g., steps the company will take on a CSR initiative). Combined with engaging visuals and playful but clear wording, bullets increase the chance the release will be noticed amid a crowded newsfeed.
